%% In this template, the places where you   %%
%% need to fill in your information are     %%
%% indicated by '???'.                      %%
%%                                          %%
%% Please do not use \input{...} to include %%
%% other tex files. Submit your LaTeX       %%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% use option [draft] for initial submission
%            [final] for the prepublication
%% `final` is omitted when `linenumbers` is requested on its own. econsocart's
%% \ProcessOptions is unstarred, so options execute in DECLARATION order, not the
%% order written here: the class declares linenumbers (:127) before draft (:131)
%% and final (:139), and both of those unconditionally overwrite the line-number
%% flag. Emitting `final` alongside `linenumbers` therefore always wins and makes
%% the option inert. `draft` still takes precedence when both are set, since draft
%% turns line numbers on anyway.
\documentclass[[-options.journal-],nameyear[# if options.draft #],draft[# elif options.linenumbers #][# else #],final[# endif #][# if options.supplement #],supplement[# endif #][# if options.seceqn #],seceqn[# endif #][# if options.linenumbers #],linenumbers[# endif #][# if doc.open_access #],openaccess[# endif #]]{econsocart}
%
%\usepackage{}
\RequirePackage[colorlinks,citecolor=blue,linkcolor=blue,urlcolor=blue,pagebackref]{hyperref}

\startlocaldefs

\newtheorem*{fact}{Fact}

%% Packages that MyST's HTML renderer supports but its LaTeX renderer does NOT
%% auto-inject (via usePackages), and that econsocart does not already provide.
%% They are loaded here so raw-LaTeX content that uses them compiles to PDF.
%% Excluded on purpose: `soul` (clashes with econsocart's \caps), `csquotes`
%% (its \enquote clashes with the qe.bst bibliography), and `algorithm2e`
%% (clashes with `algorithm`). `cleveref` is loaded near the end of the preamble
%% instead, since it must come after amsmath/amsthm/hyperref.
%% All are declared in template.yml `packages:` so jtex knows they are loaded.
\usepackage{algpseudocode}
\usepackage{subcaption}
\usepackage{multirow}
\usepackage{tabularx}
\usepackage{wrapfig}
\usepackage{threeparttable}
\usepackage{adjustbox}
\usepackage{changepage}
\usepackage{mhchem}
\usepackage{cancel}
\usepackage{supertabular}
\usepackage{epigraph}

%% Author-supplied extra packages via the `extra_packages` export option, e.g.
%%   extra_packages: tikz,pgfplots
%% for anything beyond the set above. (Do not list soul: it clashes with
%% econsocart's \caps.)
[# if options.extra_packages #]
\usepackage{[-options.extra_packages-]}
[# endif #]

%% The imports placeholder below injects the packages MyST needs for native
%% content (booktabs, longtable, graphicx, amsmath, amsthm, natbib, listings,
%% siunitx, framed, xcolor, ...), EXCEPT those already declared in
%% template.yml `packages:`. Do not add a package to `packages:` unless the
%% template (or econsocart.cls) actually loads it; declaring an unloaded
%% package suppresses MyST's injection and breaks the build.
[-IMPORTS-]

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Fix theorem numbering: MyST generates    %%
%% section-based counters (Theorem 1.1) but %%
%% QE requires global counters (Theorem 1). %%
%% \counterwithout is a LaTeX2e kernel      %%
%% command (2023-06-01 release or newer),   %%
%% not from etoolbox.                        %%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\makeatletter
\@ifundefined{c@theorem}{}{%
  \counterwithout{theorem}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@definition}{}{%
  \counterwithout{definition}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@example}{}{%
  \counterwithout{example}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@remark}{}{%
  \counterwithout{remark}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@axiom}{}{%
  \counterwithout{axiom}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@proposition}{}{%
  \counterwithout{proposition}{section}}
%% corollary is the ONE exception: MyST emits \newtheorem{corollary}{Corollary}[theorem],
%% parenting it to theorem rather than section. Sweeping it with {section} would be a
%% no-op on the reset while still stripping the \thetheorem. prefix from \thecorollary,
%% leaving every corollary in a section numbered "Corollary 1" and every cross-reference
%% to them resolving to that same string. Detach it from theorem instead.
\@ifundefined{c@corollary}{}{%
  \counterwithout{corollary}{theorem}}
\@ifundefined{c@conjecture}{}{%
  \counterwithout{conjecture}{section}}
\@ifundefined{c@observation}{}{%
  \counterwithout{observation}{section}}

\makeatother

%% myst-to-tex 1.10.1 emits \begin{assumption} and \begin{algorithm} for the
%% matching prf kinds, so both are used directly and the environments are
%% defined here. Earlier versions dropped them, which is why this template used
%% to carry them as the otherwise-unused `axiom` and `observation` kinds and
%% rename the headings; that workaround is gone, since it made the HTML output
%% say "Observation" where the PDF said "Algorithm".
%%
%% `algorithm` is deliberately a THEOREM here rather than the float from
%% \usepackage{algorithm}, which is no longer loaded. MyST emits the environment
%% with a \label and no \caption, and a float takes its number from the caption,
%% so under the float package the block rendered with no "Algorithm N" label at
%% all. Consequence to know: \begin{algorithm}...\caption{} float syntax in raw
%% LaTeX no longer compiles. Write pseudocode with the `algorithmic` environment
%% (algpseudocode, still loaded) inside a prf:algorithm block instead.
\theoremstyle{plain}
\newtheorem{assumption}{Assumption}
\newtheorem{algorithm}{Algorithm}

%% cleveref must load after amsmath, amsthm, hyperref, and the theorem
%% definitions above, so it is loaded here at the end of the preamble.
\usepackage{cleveref}

%% MyST joins multi-article exports with \include, whose implicit
%% \clearpage would start every section on a new page; a journal
%% article has no chapter breaks, so read those files with \input.
\let\include\input

%% Preprint mode strips the journal IDENTIFICATION while keeping the journal's
%% own layout, class option and bibliography style. It is orthogonal to the
%% journal choice on purpose: a Theoretical Economics preprint should be typeset
%% as Theoretical Economics with the badge removed, not silently retyped in
%% another journal's layout.
[# if options.preprint #]
\makeatletter
%% Empty the journal name in the running head via \form@runauthors, which the
%% class calls BEFORE its own \markboth, so the head keeps its normal layout and
%% draft line numbers still sit in the margin (do NOT rewrite \markboth here:
%% that drops the \hfill spacing and pushes the line-number box onto the text).
%%
%% \copyright@text keeps its \hfill for the same reason, and this one is not
%% hypothetical: defining it empty removed the glue that the head box needs, and
%% under `draft` the line-number boxes then printed ON TOP of the first-page
%% footnote block (author emails and the acknowledgement). Upstream's own draft
%% output has no such collision, so it was ours. Suppress the text, keep the
%% glue.
\def\form@runauthors{\gdef\@runjournal{}}
\def\copyright@text{\hfill}
\makeatother
[# endif #]

\endlocaldefs

\begin{document}

\begin{frontmatter}

\title{[-doc.title-]}
\runtitle{[-doc.short_title-]}

\begin{aug}
% use \particle for den|der|de|van|von (only lc!)
% [add1]{\fnms{}~\snm{}\ead[label=e?]{}}
%
%% e-mail is mandatory for each author
%
%%% initials in fnms (if any) with spaces
%
[# for author in doc.authors #]
%% The optional-argument bracket group is emitted ONLY when this author actually
%% has affiliations. A bare \author[]{...} makes econsocart look up an address
%% keyed on the empty string, which raises "Missing \endcsname inserted" and
%% "Class econsocart Error: there is no address with number", then drops the
%% affiliation line while still producing a PDF and exiting 0.
\author[# if author.affiliations #][
[#- for affiliation in author.affiliations -#]
[#- if affiliation is string -#]
[-affiliation-]
[#- else -#]
[-affiliation.id|default(affiliation)-]
[#- endif -#]
[#- if not loop.last -#],[#- endif -#]
[#- endfor -#]][# endif #]{\fnms{
[#- if author.nameParsed.given is defined -#]
[-author.nameParsed.given|trim-]
[#- elif author.name.given is defined -#]
[-author.name.given|trim-]
[#- elif author.given is defined -#]
[-author.given|trim-]
[#- else -#]
[-author.name|trim-]
[#- endif -#]}~\snm{
[#- if author.nameParsed.family is defined -#]
[-author.nameParsed.family|trim-]
[#- elif author.name.surname is defined -#]
[-author.name.surname|trim-]
[#- elif author.surname is defined -#]
[-author.surname|trim-]
[#- elif author.family is defined -#]
[-author.family|trim-]
[#- endif -#]}\ead[label=e[-loop.index-]]{[-author.email-]}}
[# endfor #]
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Addresses                                %%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% \orgdiv and its comma are emitted only for affiliations carrying a department;
%% a bare `name:` affiliation otherwise prints a stray comma.
%% See docs/template-internals.md "Authors and addresses".
[# for affiliation in doc.affiliations #]
\address[[-affiliation.id-]]{%
[# if affiliation.department|default('')|trim #]
\orgdiv{[-affiliation.department|trim-]},
[# endif #]
\orgname{[-affiliation.institution|default(affiliation.name)|default('')|trim-]}}

[# endfor #]
%% Fallback address for authors with no affiliations. econsocart defines
%% \author as \@ifnextchar[{\author@fmt}{\author@fmt[default]}, so omitting the
%% optional bracket does not skip the lookup: it substitutes the literal label
%% `default`, which the class then fails to resolve ("there is no address with
%% label: default"). Declaring an empty address under that label satisfies the
%% lookup. Emitted unconditionally because it is inert when unused: a document
%% where every author is affiliated produces byte-identical PDF text with and
%% without it, so this costs nothing rather than needing a per-document guard.
\address[default]{}

\end{aug}

[# if not options.supplement #]
%% Put support info here
[# if parts.acknowledgement #]
\begin{funding}
[-parts.acknowledgement-]
\end{funding}
[# endif #]
%
%% Suppressed in preprint mode. The placeholder asserts that a co-editor handled
%% the manuscript, which is exactly the journal-submission signal `preprint` exists
%% to strip: a working paper posted publicly would otherwise read "Co-editor [Name
%% Surname; will be inserted later] handled this manuscript."
[# if not options.preprint #]
\coeditor{\fnm{[Name} \snm{Surname}; will be inserted later]}
[# endif #]
[# endif #]

[# if parts.abstract #]
\begin{abstract}
[-parts.abstract-]
\end{abstract}
[# endif #]

[# if not options.supplement #]
\begin{keyword}
[# if doc.keywords #]
[# for kw in doc.keywords #]
\kwd{[-kw|trim-]}
[# endfor #]
[# endif #]
\end{keyword}

%% Omit the block entirely when there are no codes, rather than emitting an
%% empty one: the class prints its "JEL CLASSIFICATION" label regardless of
%% content, so an empty block renders as a stray label with dangling punctuation.
%% Econometrica does not use JEL codes: upstream ecta_sample.tex carries no JEL
%% block, while qe_sample.tex and te_sample.tex each carry one. So the block is
%% suppressed under `journal: ecta` even when the document supplies `tags`, which
%% lets one source retarget across all three journals without hand-editing.
%% The suppression is deliberately NOT silent: the trace below survives into the
%% .tex so a reader can see codes were withheld rather than lost.
[# if doc.tags #]
[# if options.journal == "ecta" #]
%% JEL codes present in the document frontmatter were omitted here: Econometrica
%% house style carries no JEL classification block. They still appear in the qe
%% and te exports of this same source.
[# else #]
\begin{keyword}[class=JEL] %% alphabetical order
[# for code in doc.tags #]
\kwd{[-code|trim-]}
[# endfor #]
\end{keyword}
[# endif #]
[# endif #]
[# endif #]

\end{frontmatter}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%%%% Main text entry area:
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

[-CONTENT-]

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Appendix                                 %%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% There is deliberately no `parts.appendix` branch here. BECAUSE there is none,
%% a document that still declares `parts: appendix:` loses its appendix ENTIRELY
%% and silently: MyST logs "Built <doc>#parts.appendix", then the content reaches
%% neither this .tex nor the PDF, with no warning and exit 0. Do not look for a
%% missing bibliography entry as the symptom; there is none.
%% The branch was removed rather than kept because of the underlying MyST
%% behavior: harvesting walks the RENDERED document and frontmatter parts are
%% excluded from it ("Content within these parts is not rendered in the
%% document", per docs/document-parts), so a reference cited only in a part
%% reached this .tex while its entry never reached the .bib, leaving an undefined
%% citation. A branch producing wrong bibliographies was not better than an
%% obvious empty space.
%% Open and close the appendix in the document body instead, which keeps the
%% content in the main AST so its citations are harvested:
%%     ```{raw} latex
%%     \begin{appendix}
%%     ```
%%     :::{include} appendix.md
%%     :::
%%     ```{raw} latex
%%     \end{appendix}
%%     ```
%% Headings in the included file must be `#` level. Included content sits one
%% level below the surrounding sections, and a demoted heading does not pick up
%% the class's appendix prefix, printing ".1" instead of "APPENDIX A:".
%% Known cost on the HTML side: MyST parses each raw block and renders the
%% environment NAME as a paragraph, so the website shows a stray paragraph
%% reading "appendix" at each end. The PDF is unaffected.
%% See README "Appendices". Nothing currently checks this automatically: verify
%% by grepping the emitted main.bib for every key cited in the emitted .tex.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Bibliography:  BibTeX Version          %%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Each Econometric Society journal ships its own BibTeX style for ARTICLES:
%% Econometrica uses econsoc, Quantitative Economics uses qe, Theoretical
%% Economics uses te. `preprint` is orthogonal and does NOT change the style: a
%% Theoretical Economics preprint keeps the te style, an Econometrica
%% preprint keeps econsoc. All three bst files are vendored and listed in
%% template.yml.
%%
%% Supplements deliberately use the same style. Upstream's qe_supp_template.tex
%% and te_supp_template.tex still say ecta-fullname, but that is a stale
%% reference, not a target to match: ecta-fullname.bst only ever existed in the
%% Econometrica repository, which DELETED it on 2026-03-06 (commit 959c321) and
%% added econsoc.bst in the same commit. The qe and te supplement templates were
%% last touched 2025-03-03, a year before that removal, and neither repository
%% ever shipped the file. Following them would mean shipping a retired style.
[# if doc.bibliography #]
\bibliographystyle{[# if options.journal == "ecta" #]econsoc[# elif options.journal == "te" #]te[# else #]qe[# endif #]} % Style BST file
\bibliography{[-doc.bibliography-]}  % Bibliography file (usually '*.bib')
[# else #]
%% NOTE: User has not specified a bibliography file in frontmatter.
%% If you want to use BibTeX, please specify 'bibliography: <your_bib_file.bib>'
%% in your document's frontmatter.
[# endif #]

\end{document}
